title: Introduce dynamic sampling governor for high-QPS services
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Several high-QPS frontend and runtime services incur measurable CPU and network overhead from always-on trace emission. This increases cost on Dedicated clusters and creates noisy metrics for downstream trace storage. Tail-based sampling work reduced some cost, but we still see hot services generating large numbers of short, low-value spans. Goal: implement a dynamic sampling governor that reduces tracer-side overhead while preserving fidelity for errors and latency tails.

Proposed solution:
- Client-side governor daemon in the tracer that computes a per-service sample probability in real-time. Input signals: recent QPS, average spans per request, 95/99/99.9th latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), configured priority for the route.
- Fast-path decision: in the hot path the tracer uses a single atomic integer and two bitmasks (decision cache + forced-sample flag) to avoid allocations and locks. Decision is lookup-only for the majority of requests.
- Token-bucket cap: maintain a lightweight token bucket per-process to limit absolute sampled traces per second to a cluster-level budget.
- Tail-preservation: integrate with the collector-side prefiltering hook so any trace that crosses a latency or error threshold in the collector is upsampled (always stored) even if client sampling dropped it. Also emit a lightweight out-of-band signal (span_meta) for traces to be considered for tail sampling without full payload.
- Adaptive sensitivity: a PID-inspired controller nudges sample probability based on moving-window delta of observed tail count vs target. Initial target: 0.5% of requests sampled for hot endpoints, adjustable by route config.
- Telemetry: expose metrics per-service: sampling_probability, sampled_count, dropped_count, tokens_remaining, tracer_cpu_ns_total, avg_bytes_per_trace. Dashboards: new panels for sampling_rate vs errors, kv-cache hit ratio vs sampled_rate, and tracer CPU overhead.

Implementation plan:
1) PoC: implement governor library patch (+ compatibility shim) and a collector hook to accept lightweight metadata. (2 weeks)
2) Benchmarks: microbench with 1k/5k/10k RPS profiles to measure overhead and sampling accuracy. (1 week)
3) Canary rollout: enable on 5 non-critical services (internal infra) with strict alerts on error rate and apdex regression. (1 week)
4) Full rollout with per-customer opt-outs and runtime feature flag.

Rollout safety: default to conservative sampling (higher sample rate) in first two cycles. If any service observes >0.2% increase in 99th latency or >1% regression in error rate for 10 minutes, automatic rollback via feature flag.

Success metrics: reduce tracer CPU overhead for top-10 QPS services by >=70% while preserving >=95% recall of error traces and <1% change in 99.9th latency. Reduce trace ingress bytes by >60% on Dedicated clusters.

Open questions/risks:
- Collector-side upsampling requires non-trivial changes to trace ingestion pipeline; need infra capacity for metadata-only signals.
- Edge-case: very short-lived requests that only produce a single tiny span — sampling may remove useful signals unless we tag errors at the client.
- Interaction with existing tail-based sampling work (ENG-14102) — need clear ownership and migration plan.

Deliverables: PR for tracer library, collector hook PR, bench reports, dashboard panels, rollout playbook, and a follow-up ticket for configuration UI in Console.
